title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #6

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.

2. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. pascal (Pa)

3. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 50 °C

5. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

6. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Milk souring
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Paper burning to ash

7. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Heat.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.

2. B — newton (N)

3. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

4. B — 100 °C

5. C — Producers

6. A — Ice melting to water

7. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

8. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.

10. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.

11. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Properties of Matter; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Light; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Heat; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
